question: m04
q: Is unemployment higher in NSW or Victoria right now, and by how much?

transcript.answer:
Unemployment is higher in **Victoria**. In September 2026, the latest month available, it was **5.1%** in Victoria and **4.7%** in NSW, so Victoria was about **0.3 percentage points higher**. Unrounded, the figures are 5.05% and 4.71%, a gap of 0.34 points. These are seasonally adjusted ABS Labour Force rates.

The gap has closed a lot in a short time:

| Month (2026) | NSW | Victoria | How much higher in Victoria |
|---|---|---|---|
| April | 4.4% | 4.8% | 0.4 pts |
| May | 4.3% | 4.9% | 0.6 pts |
| June | 4.0% | 5.1% | 1.1 pts |
| July | 4.3% | 5.1% | 0.8 pts |
| August | 4.4% | 5.2% | 0.8 pts |
| September | 4.7% | 5.1% | 0.3 pts |

- **NSW** rose sharply in September, up about 0.35 points from August to its highest level in this six-month period.
- **Victoria** dipped slightly, by about 0.1 points.

State figures jump around a lot from month to month, so one month's change in NSW could be partly noise. Even so, Victoria has had the higher rate in every month shown.
